noteAppend: Paediatric, penicillin-allergy, CKD and CLD lines added 21 Oct 2026 (batch 01) from standard product-label (US PI / UK SmPC) and BNF dosing; individual labels were not re-opened for this batch. Pharmacist verification required; clinical review pending.
paediatricRowText: This row gives the paediatric dose.

drugs.ckd: Oral: CrCl below 30 mL/min — do not use 875/125 mg tablets; 10–30 mL/min usual (weight-based in children) dose every 12 h, adults 500/125 mg; below 10 mL/min every 24 h. IV 1.2 g (adults): CrCl 10–30 mL/min 1.2 g then 600 mg every 12 h; below 10 mL/min 1.2 g then 600 mg every 24 h (product label).
drugs.cld: Cholestatic jaundice risk: monitor LFTs; contraindicated after previous co-amoxiclav-associated jaundice or hepatic dysfunction (product label).

drugs.ckd: CrCl 10–30 mL/min: give the usual (weight-based in children) dose every 12 h; below 10 mL/min: every 24 h; adult maximum 500 mg per dose at these levels. IV high-dose (meningitis): reduce the frequency with pharmacist advice (product label).
drugs.cld: No dose change.

drugs.ckd: CrCl 10–50 mL/min: give every 6–12 h; below 10 mL/min: every 12–24 h (product label).
drugs.cld: No dose change.

drugs.ckd: Single pre-hospital or loading dose: no change. Repeated high doses with CrCl below 10 mL/min: reduce the dose (neurotoxicity risk) (BNF).
drugs.cld: No dose change.

drugs.ckd: No dose change for single IM doses.
drugs.cld: No dose change.

drugs.ckd: CrCl below 10 mL/min: maximum 1 g every 8 h (BNF).
drugs.cld: Cholestatic hepatitis risk (can occur up to 2 months after stopping): avoid after previous flucloxacillin-associated jaundice; use with caution in hepatic impairment (BNF).

drugs.ckd: CrCl 20–40 mL/min: 2.25 g every 6 h (3.375 g every 6 h for nosocomial pneumonia); below 20 mL/min: 2.25 g every 8 h (2.25 g every 6 h for nosocomial pneumonia); haemodialysis: 2.25 g every 12 h plus 0.75 g after each session (product label).
drugs.cld: No dose change.

drugs.ckd: CrCl 30–59 mL/min: maximum 1 g/day; 15–29 mL/min: 250 mg every 8–12 h; 5–14 mL/min: 250 mg every 24 h (product label).
drugs.cld: No dose change.

drugs.ckd: Single prophylactic dose: no change. Repeated dosing: CrCl 11–34 mL/min half dose every 12 h; 10 mL/min or below half dose every 18–24 h (product label).
drugs.cld: No dose change.

drugs.ckd: Oral: CrCl 10–29 mL/min standard dose every 24 h; below 10 mL/min every 48 h (product label).
drugs.cld: No dose change.

drugs.ckd: IV: CrCl 10–20 mL/min 750 mg every 12 h; below 10 mL/min 750 mg every 24 h (product label).
drugs.cld: No dose change.

drugs.ckd: CrCl below 20 mL/min: halve the dose (product label).
drugs.cld: No dose change.

drugs.ckd: No dose change if liver function is normal; CrCl below 10 mL/min: maximum 2 g/day — for meningitis doses take pharmacist advice and monitor levels (product information).
drugs.cld: No dose change if renal function is normal; combined severe renal and hepatic impairment: monitor plasma levels (product information).

drugs.ckd: CrCl 30 mL/min or below (including haemodialysis): 500 mg once daily (product label).
drugs.cld: No dose change.

drugs.ckd: CrCl 26–50 mL/min: standard dose every 12 h; 10–25 mL/min: half dose every 12 h; below 10 mL/min: half dose every 24 h (product label).
drugs.cld: No dose change.

drugs.ckd: For 500 mg every 6 h: CrCl 60–89 mL/min 400 mg every 6 h; 30–59 mL/min 300 mg every 6 h; 15–29 mL/min 200 mg every 6 h; below 15 mL/min only if haemodialysis is started within 48 h. Seizure risk rises with renal impairment (product label).
drugs.cld: No dose change.

drugs.ckd: Full loading dose, then maintenance halved at CrCl 10–30 mL/min and quartered below 10 mL/min (product label).
drugs.cld: No dose change; monitor LFTs.

drugs.ckd: Loading dose unchanged; maintenance by AUC or trough monitoring with interval extended for renal function; haemodialysis — dose after sessions by level (product label; pharmacy TDM).
drugs.cld: No dose change.

drugs.ckd: Loading unchanged; from day 4: CrCl 30–80 mL/min half the dose (or full dose every 48 h); below 30 mL/min one third (or every 72 h) (product SmPC).
drugs.cld: No dose change.

drugs.ckd: Single prophylactic dose: no change. Repeated dosing: extend the interval by creatinine clearance with level monitoring; avoid if CrCl below 20 mL/min unless specialist-supervised (product label; pharmacy TDM).
drugs.cld: No dose change.

drugs.ckd: No dose change (product label).
drugs.cld: No dose change; monitor LFTs in severe hepatic disease during prolonged courses (product label).

drugs.ckd: No dose change; haemodialysis — give the dose after the session (product label).
drugs.cld: Severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh C): reduce the dose by 50% (product label).

drugs.ckd: No dose change.
drugs.cld: No standard dose change; use with caution and avoid other hepatotoxic drugs where possible (product label).

drugs.ckd: Avoid in renal impairment — use doxycycline instead (BNF: tetracyclines other than doxycycline and minocycline can worsen renal failure).
drugs.cld: Use with caution (BNF).

drugs.ckd: CrCl below 30 mL/min: reduce the dose by 50% (product label).
drugs.cld: No dose change if renal function is normal; avoid with combined severe hepatic and renal impairment (product label).

drugs.ckd: No dose change; caution if CrCl below 10 mL/min (product label).
drugs.cld: Hepatotoxicity reported: check LFTs and stop if hepatitis develops (product label).

drugs.ckd: Severe renal impairment: maximum 1.5 g/day (ototoxicity risk) (BNF).
drugs.cld: Hepatotoxicity risk: use with caution; avoid in severe hepatic impairment (BNF).

drugs.ckd: Oral: CrCl 30–50 mL/min 250–500 mg every 12 h; below 30 mL/min 250–500 mg every 18 h. IV: CrCl 5–29 mL/min 200–400 mg every 18–24 h (product label).
drugs.cld: No dose change.

drugs.ckd: For 500 mg every 12 h: CrCl 20–50 mL/min 500 mg then 250 mg every 12 h; 10–19 mL/min 500 mg then 125 mg every 12 h; below 10 mL/min 500 mg then 125 mg every 24 h (product SmPC).
drugs.cld: No dose change.

drugs.ckd: CrCl 15–30 mL/min: 50% of the dose; below 15 mL/min: avoid (product label).
drugs.cld: Avoid in severe hepatic impairment (product label).

drugs.ckd: eGFR below 15 mL/min: avoid unless no alternative (ULHT renal guide 2018); monitor levels.
drugs.cld: Reduce the dose and monitor plasma levels; avoid in severe hepatic impairment (marrow toxicity) (BNF).

drugs.ckd: Topical/ophthalmic use: no systemic dose adjustment.
drugs.cld: Topical/ophthalmic use: no systemic dose adjustment.

drugs.ckd: No dose change (product label).
drugs.cld: No dose change in mild to moderate impairment; severe impairment not studied — monitor platelets (product label).

drugs.ckd: Treatment: CrCl 30–60 mL/min 30 mg twice daily; 10–30 mL/min 30 mg once daily; haemodialysis 30 mg after each session (product label).
drugs.cld: No dose change in mild to moderate impairment (product label).

drugs.ckd: IV: CrCl 25–50 mL/min standard dose every 12 h; 10–25 mL/min every 24 h; below 10 mL/min 50% dose every 24 h; keep well hydrated (product label).
drugs.cld: No dose change.

drugs.ckd: Contraindicated in severe renal impairment; reduce the dose or extend the interval in moderate impairment (product label).
drugs.cld: Contraindicated in cirrhosis or marked hepatic disease (risk of hepatic encephalopathy) (product label).

drugs.ckd: Topical/ophthalmic use: no systemic dose adjustment.
drugs.cld: Topical/ophthalmic use: no systemic dose adjustment.

drugs.ckd: eGFR 30–60 mL/min: start 50 mg daily; 15–30 mL/min: 50 mg every other day; titrate to urate (product label).
drugs.cld: Reduce the dose; check LFTs early in treatment (product label).

drugs.ckd: No dose change.
drugs.cld: Use with caution; avoid in severe hepatic impairment (BNF).

drugs.ckd: Avoid in severe renal impairment (CrCl below 10 mL/min) (product label).
drugs.cld: Avoid in severe hepatic impairment (bleeding risk) (BNF).

drugs.ckd: No data in renal impairment; use with caution (product SmPC).
drugs.cld: No data in hepatic impairment; use with caution (product SmPC).

drugs.ckd: No dose change.
drugs.cld: No standard dose change; monitor for fluid retention and glucose.

drugs.ckd: No dose change.
drugs.cld: Severe hepatic impairment increases budesonide exposure: use the lowest effective dose (product label).

drugs.ckd: Avoid if eGFR below 30 mL/min; use the lowest dose with monitoring in milder impairment (product SmPC).
drugs.cld: Avoid in severe hepatic impairment (product SmPC).

drugs.ckd: CrCl below 30 mL/min: prophylaxis 20 mg once daily (UK SmPC) / 30 mg once daily (US label); treatment 1 mg/kg once daily (product label).
drugs.cld: Use with caution: bleeding risk with coagulopathy (product label).

drugs.ckd: No dose change in an emergency.
drugs.cld: No dose change in an emergency.

drugs.ckd: No dose change.
drugs.cld: Contraindicated in severe hepatic impairment (product SmPC).

drugs.ckd: No dose change.
drugs.cld: Moderate or severe hepatic impairment: maximum 5 mg in 24 h (product label).

drugs.ckd: Contraindicated if CrCl below 15 mL/min; maximum 2.5 mg in 24 h with milder impairment (product label).
drugs.cld: Contraindicated in severe hepatic impairment; maximum 2.5 mg in 24 h in mild to moderate impairment (product label).

drugs.ckd: Use with caution (product label).
drugs.cld: Oral maximum single dose 50 mg in mild to moderate hepatic impairment; contraindicated in severe impairment (product label).

drugs.ckd: Avoid in severe renal impairment; use the lowest dose with monitoring in milder impairment (product label).
drugs.cld: Avoid in severe hepatic impairment (product label).

drugs.ckd: Avoid if CrCl below 30 mL/min (product label).
drugs.cld: Use the lowest effective dose; avoid in severe hepatic impairment (product label).

drugs.ckd: Avoid in renal impairment (and in pregnancy from 20 weeks, as noted) (product label).
drugs.cld: Use with caution; avoid in severe hepatic impairment (product label).

drugs.ckd: Contraindicated in advanced renal impairment or volume depletion; use the lower dose range in milder impairment (product label).
drugs.cld: Use with caution; stop if LFTs rise (product label).

drugs.ckd: Severe renal impairment: start at 10 mg daily and titrate (product SmPC).
drugs.cld: Contraindicated in hepatic impairment (product SmPC).

drugs.ckd: No dose change.
drugs.cld: No dose change.

drugs.ckd: No dose change for local infiltration.
drugs.cld: Use the lowest volume; amide anaesthetics accumulate in severe liver disease (product label).

drugs.ckd: Oliguria or raised creatinine: reduce or stop the maintenance infusion and monitor serum magnesium and reflexes (product label).
drugs.cld: No dose change.

drugs.ckd: CrCl 60 mL/min or below: halve the dose; end-stage kidney disease: quarter of the dose (product label).
drugs.cld: Child-Pugh B or C: halve the dose (product label).

drugs.ckd: Start lower and extend the interval; avoid repeated dosing in severe impairment (metabolite accumulation) (product label).
drugs.cld: Reduce the dose; avoid in hepatic encephalopathy (product label).

drugs.ckd: No dose change.
drugs.cld: Start at a lower dose and monitor blood pressure in hepatic impairment (product label).

drugs.ckd: No dose change; renal data limited (product label).
drugs.cld: Cirrhosis: 30 mg every 4 h with close blood pressure and heart rate monitoring (product label).

drugs.ckd: No dose change.
drugs.cld: Severe hepatic impairment: maximum 8 mg/day (product label).

drugs.ckd: Not applicable.
drugs.cld: Not applicable.

drugs.ckd: No dose change; watch for water intoxication with prolonged infusion (product label).
drugs.cld: No dose change.

drugs.ckd: IV: CrCl 30 mL/min or below — give at least 6 h apart (product label).
drugs.cld: Hepatic impairment, chronic alcohol use or weight below 50 kg: maximum 3 g/day (lower for weight-based dosing); avoid in severe active liver disease (product label).

drugs.ckd: Contraindicated in significant renal impairment (product label).
drugs.cld: No dose change.

drugs.ckd: No dose change; start low (product label).
drugs.cld: Reduce the dose in hepatic impairment (reduced first-pass metabolism) (product label).

drugs.ckd: Not applicable — dose by INR and weight.
drugs.cld: Not applicable — dose by INR and weight; note the existing contraindication in this row.

drugs.ckd: No dose change.
drugs.cld: Severe hepatic impairment: oral maximum 20 mg/day; use the infusion with caution (product label).

drugs.ckd: No dose change.
drugs.cld: Contraindicated in moderate or severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh B or C) (product label).

drugs.ckd: No dose change.
drugs.cld: No dose change.

drugs.ckd: No dose change if CrCl is 10 mL/min or above; not studied below 10 mL/min (product label).
drugs.cld: Not studied in severe hepatic impairment (product label).

drugs.ckd: Not recommended if serum creatinine is 5 mg/dL (442 µmol/L) or above (product label).
drugs.cld: Not applicable — used for variceal bleeding in liver disease.

drugs.ckd: CrCl 60 mL/min or below: monitor for anticholinergic effects (product label).
drugs.cld: No dose change in mild to moderate impairment (product label).

drugs.ckd: CrCl below 70 mL/min: halve the dose (product label).
drugs.cld: Use with caution (product label).

drugs.ckd: IV: serum creatinine 120–249 µmol/L 10 mg/kg twice daily; 250–500 µmol/L 10 mg/kg daily; above 500 µmol/L 5 mg/kg daily (product SmPC).
drugs.cld: No dose change.

drugs.ckd: No dose change; dose by aPTT (product label).
drugs.cld: Bleeding risk with coagulopathy; dose by aPTT (product label).

drugs.ckd: No dose change; free fraction rises — monitor clinically (product label).
drugs.cld: Contraindicated in hepatic disease (as noted in this row) (product label).

drugs.ckd: No dose change.
drugs.cld: Severe hepatic impairment: give 20–30% of the usual dose (product label).

Acne Vulgaris.paediatric: Young people 12 years and over: adult doses apply (NICE NG198 covers this age group); under 12 years: specialist dermatology.
Acne Vulgaris.allergyAlternative: Not applicable — no beta-lactam in this topic.

Acute Appendicitis.paediatric: Adult-only topic — use the paediatric pathway.
Acute Appendicitis.allergyAlternative: Severe beta-lactam allergy: ciprofloxacin 400 mg IV every 12 h plus metronidazole 500 mg IV every 8 h (IDSA intra-abdominal infection guidance).

Acute Cholecystitis: Admission and Surgi.paediatric: Adult-only topic — use the paediatric pathway.
Acute Cholecystitis: Admission and Surgi.allergyAlternative: Ciprofloxacin plus metronidazole (the ciprofloxacin row in this topic).

Acute Exacerbation of COPD.paediatric: Adult-only topic — use the paediatric pathway.
Acute Exacerbation of COPD.allergyAlternative: Doxycycline (the doxycycline row in this topic).

Acute Mesenteric Ischaemia: Recognition.paediatric: Adult-only topic — use the paediatric pathway.
Acute Mesenteric Ischaemia: Recognition.allergyAlternative: Ciprofloxacin 400 mg IV every 12 h plus metronidazole 500 mg IV every 8 h (IDSA intra-abdominal infection guidance).

Acute Otitis Media: Antibiotic Prescribi.paediatric: Children: see the paediatric rows of this topic (NICE NG91).
Acute Otitis Media: Antibiotic Prescribi.allergyAlternative: Clarithromycin; erythromycin in pregnancy (NICE NG91 — rows in this topic).

Acute Pyelonephritis in Pregnancy: Asses.paediatric: Not applicable — maternity topic; neonatal care follows the neonatal pathway.
Acute Pyelonephritis in Pregnancy: Asses.allergyAlternative: History of anaphylaxis or other immediate reaction to penicillin: avoid cephalosporins and get urgent microbiology advice — NICE NG111 gives no non-beta-lactam option in pregnancy.

Acute Red Eye: Conjunctivitis versus Ang.paediatric: Adult-only topic — use the paediatric pathway.
Acute Red Eye: Conjunctivitis versus Ang.allergyAlternative: Not applicable — no beta-lactam in this topic.

Acute Upper Gastrointestinal Bleeding.paediatric: Adult-only topic — use the paediatric pathway.
Acute Upper Gastrointestinal Bleeding.allergyAlternative: Severe beta-lactam allergy: ciprofloxacin (MOH, as noted in the ceftriaxone row).

Adult Upper-Airway Emergency: Stridor, E.paediatric: Adult-only topic — use the paediatric pathway.
Adult Upper-Airway Emergency: Stridor, E.allergyAlternative: Severe beta-lactam allergy: seek microbiology advice before the first dose (existing row).

Cataract Surgery Assessment and Preparat.paediatric: Adult-only topic — use the paediatric pathway.
Cataract Surgery Assessment and Preparat.allergyAlternative: Intracameral moxifloxacin instead of cefazolin (ophthalmology prophylaxis practice).

Cellulitis and Erysipelas: Outpatient ve.paediatric: Adult-only topic — use the paediatric pathway.
Cellulitis and Erysipelas: Outpatient ve.allergyAlternative: Oral: doxycycline or clindamycin; IV: clindamycin, or vancomycin for severe or MRSA-risk infection (MOH SSTI — rows in this topic).

Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease.paediatric: Adult-only topic — use the paediatric pathway.
Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease.allergyAlternative: Not applicable — no beta-lactam in this topic.

Community-Acquired Pneumonia.paediatric: Adult-only topic — use the paediatric pathway.
Community-Acquired Pneumonia.allergyAlternative: Levofloxacin 750 mg daily or moxifloxacin 400 mg daily after excluding TB (MOH LRTI).

Deep Neck Space Infections and Quinsy: A.paediatric: Adult-only topic — use the paediatric pathway.
Deep Neck Space Infections and Quinsy: A.allergyAlternative: Clindamycin 450 mg IV then oral (the clindamycin row in this topic).

Diabetic Foot Infection: Urgent Assessme.paediatric: Adult-only topic — use the paediatric pathway.
Diabetic Foot Infection: Urgent Assessme.allergyAlternative: Mild: clarithromycin, erythromycin (pregnancy) or doxycycline; moderate or severe: co-trimoxazole with or without gentamicin and/or metronidazole (NICE NG19).

Diabetic Foot: Risk Stratification and U.paediatric: Adult-only topic — use the paediatric pathway.
Diabetic Foot: Risk Stratification and U.allergyAlternative: Mild: clarithromycin, erythromycin (pregnancy) or doxycycline; moderate or severe: co-trimoxazole with or without gentamicin and/or metronidazole (NICE NG19).

Elective Cholecystectomy Pre-operative A.paediatric: Adult-only topic — use the paediatric pathway.
Elective Cholecystectomy Pre-operative A.allergyAlternative: Clindamycin 900 mg IV plus ciprofloxacin 400 mg IV (rows in this topic).

Elective Coronary Revascularisation Revi.paediatric: Adult-only topic — use the paediatric pathway.
Elective Coronary Revascularisation Revi.allergyAlternative: Clindamycin 900 mg IV (the clindamycin row in this topic).

Elective Hernia Repair Assessment.paediatric: Adult-only topic — use the paediatric pathway.
Elective Hernia Repair Assessment.allergyAlternative: Clindamycin 900 mg IV, or vancomycin 15 mg/kg (rows in this topic).

Elective Hip and Knee Arthroplasty Prepa.paediatric: Adult-only topic — use the paediatric pathway.
Elective Hip and Knee Arthroplasty Prepa.allergyAlternative: Clindamycin 900 mg IV, or vancomycin 15 mg/kg (rows in this topic).

Elective Hysterectomy for Benign Disease.paediatric: Adult-only topic — use the paediatric pathway.
Elective Hysterectomy for Benign Disease.allergyAlternative: Clindamycin 900 mg IV plus gentamicin 5 mg/kg (rows in this topic).

Elective Valve Intervention Assessment.paediatric: Adult-only topic — use the paediatric pathway.
Elective Valve Intervention Assessment.allergyAlternative: Clindamycin 900 mg IV (the clindamycin row in this topic).

Fournier Gangrene: Recognition, Resuscit.paediatric: Adult-only topic — use the paediatric pathway.
Fournier Gangrene: Recognition, Resuscit.allergyAlternative: Clindamycin or metronidazole with an aminoglycoside or a fluoroquinolone, plus vancomycin (IDSA SSTI 2014).

Group B Streptococcus: Risk-Based Intrap.paediatric: Not applicable — maternity topic; neonatal care follows the neonatal pathway.
Group B Streptococcus: Risk-Based Intrap.allergyAlternative: Non-severe allergy: cefuroxime; history of anaphylaxis: vancomycin (rows in this topic).

Headache: Red Flags and Primary Headache.paediatric: Adult-only topic — use the paediatric pathway.
Headache: Red Flags and Primary Headache.allergyAlternative: Bacterial meningitis with severe beta-lactam allergy: aztreonam with trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole and vancomycin (MOH — row in this topic).

Infective Endocarditis: Recognition, Blo.paediatric: Adult-only topic — use the paediatric pathway.
Infective Endocarditis: Recognition, Blo.allergyAlternative: Vancomycin (the vancomycin row in this topic; ESC 2023).

Kidney Stones: Urology Referral and Prev.paediatric: Adult-only topic — use the paediatric pathway.
Kidney Stones: Urology Referral and Prev.allergyAlternative: Meropenem has under 1% cross-reactivity; after penicillin anaphylaxis get microbiology advice.

Maternal Sepsis in Pregnancy or Postpart.paediatric: Not applicable — maternity topic; neonatal care follows the neonatal pathway.
Maternal Sepsis in Pregnancy or Postpart.allergyAlternative: Clindamycin plus gentamicin, with vancomycin if MRSA is suspected (rows in this topic).

Metabolic and Bariatric Surgery Evaluati.paediatric: Adult-only topic — use the paediatric pathway.
Metabolic and Bariatric Surgery Evaluati.allergyAlternative: Clindamycin 900 mg IV plus ciprofloxacin 400 mg IV (MOH).

Perineal Tear: Assessment and Repair.paediatric: Not applicable — maternity topic; neonatal care follows the neonatal pathway.
Perineal Tear: Assessment and Repair.allergyAlternative: Clindamycin (the clindamycin row in this topic).

Perineal Tear: Postpartum Care and Follo.paediatric: Not applicable — maternity topic; neonatal care follows the neonatal pathway.
Perineal Tear: Postpartum Care and Follo.allergyAlternative: Clindamycin with metronidazole as in the repair topic; avoid co-amoxiclav.

Prelabour Rupture of Membranes.paediatric: Not applicable — maternity topic; neonatal care follows the neonatal pathway.
Prelabour Rupture of Membranes.allergyAlternative: Erythromycin, or clindamycin plus gentamicin (rows in this topic).

Preterm Labour and Threatened Preterm Bi.paediatric: Not applicable — maternity topic; neonatal care follows the neonatal pathway.
Preterm Labour and Threatened Preterm Bi.allergyAlternative: Group B Streptococcus prophylaxis: cefuroxime for non-severe allergy; vancomycin 1 g IV after anaphylaxis (as in the GBS topic).

Severe Community-Acquired Pneumonia: Sev.paediatric: Adult-only topic — use the paediatric pathway.
Severe Community-Acquired Pneumonia: Sev.allergyAlternative: Levofloxacin (the levofloxacin row in this topic).

Sexually Transmitted Infection Screening.paediatric: Adolescents: adult doses apply (CDC STI 2021); younger children: use the paediatric pathway and safeguarding.
Sexually Transmitted Infection Screening.allergyAlternative: Syphilis, not pregnant: doxycycline 100 mg twice daily for 14 days; pregnancy: penicillin desensitisation. Gonorrhoea with cephalosporin allergy: gentamicin 240 mg IM plus azithromycin 2 g orally (CDC STI 2021).

Suspected Meningitis and Encephalitis: E.paediatric: Adult-only topic — use the paediatric pathway.
Suspected Meningitis and Encephalitis: E.allergyAlternative: Chloramphenicol; meropenem for non-anaphylactic severe allergy (rows in this topic).

Suspected Meningitis: Community Recognit.paediatric: Child doses for benzylpenicillin are in that row; cephalosporin doses for children: use the paediatric pathway.
Suspected Meningitis: Community Recognit.allergyAlternative: History of anaphylaxis to penicillin: do not give benzylpenicillin; give ceftriaxone or cefotaxime unless there is also cephalosporin anaphylaxis, otherwise transfer without antibiotic (NICE NG240).

Vaginal Birth After Caesarean: Antenatal.paediatric: Not applicable — maternity topic; neonatal care follows the neonatal pathway.
Vaginal Birth After Caesarean: Antenatal.allergyAlternative: Clindamycin 900 mg IV before incision (caesarean prophylaxis).

Vaginal Birth After Caesarean: Intrapart.paediatric: Not applicable — maternity topic; neonatal care follows the neonatal pathway.
Vaginal Birth After Caesarean: Intrapart.allergyAlternative: Clindamycin 900 mg IV before incision (caesarean prophylaxis).
